quote: > **`hook`** writes nothing to stderr and always exits 0. **`mcp`** writes only MCP frames on stdout. Neither has a human design surface.

moves.claim: `hook` and `mcp` are Unix clients under the new directory and euid checks, so a refused directory or a mismatched peer must reach `hook` only as a fail-open with no stderr and exit 0, and must put nothing but MCP frames on `mcp`'s stdout.

quote: > NEVER skip spans or events on the 6 must-trace paths (Section 4). The agent loses its ability to debug.

moves.claim: The new refusals fall on the must-trace `viola run` start and `wait` / `last` paths, so each must keep the span and event those paths owe wherever a line is admitted.

quote: > NEVER write to stderr from `viola hook`, and NEVER exit non-zero from it, including on security-check failures.

moves.claim: A refusal of this chunk must reach `hook` with no stderr byte and exit 0.

quote: > NEVER expose absolute paths in any external error.

moves.claim: Each new refusal's external text must hold no socket-directory path on any surface.

quote: > NEVER echo serde_path_to_error drift reports or anyhow chains into MCP `structuredContent` or channel `error.data`

moves.claim: `bind_endpoint`'s failure must leave its anyhow chain behind when it becomes a closed refusal, none of it reaching an external result.

quote: > NEVER write to stderr from `viola hook`, and NEVER exit non-zero from it, including on security-check failures.

moves.claim: The per-user directory must be verified by `lstat` before bind and before any client connect, a failure refusing on each surface as stated, with the refusal given the code owed here and the socket chmodded 0600 after the bind as the secondary control only.

quote: > NEVER expose absolute paths in any external error.

moves.claim: A CLI verb meeting a peer euid mismatch or a refused directory must write no frame and exit 21 in both modes with a closed `detail` and a fixed hint in this form, whichever code the plan settles, after the client's exit-13 refusals and the strict-modes refusal.

quote: > NEVER expose absolute paths in any external error.

moves.claim: Each new `instance-unreachable` cause must be a code word on both readers, or it reads `unknown` or null, and each refusal's external text must hold a fixed message with no path, type name or anyhow chain.

quote: > NEVER write to stderr from `viola hook`, and NEVER exit non-zero from it, including on security-check failures.

moves.claim: `hook` is a Unix client that takes the new checks, and any refusal of this chunk must reach it only as this fail-open: exit 0, no body, no stderr and no frame.
